technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot as the runtime framework for Spring XD modules, leveraging the existing Spring XD module infrastructure (sources, sinks, processors) for the new features.
Use Apache Kafka's AdminClient and ConsumerRebalanceListener for partition pre-allocation and offset management (U2, U3, U4).

Persist Kafka source offsets in a durable store (e.g., the XD file/DB-based offset store) so that progress survives container restarts and that undeployment/redeployment replays from the configured start offset.
For the message bus partition pre-allocation (U4), use a static assignment strategy at deployment time computed by the stream deployer, rather than letting Kafka rebalance dynamically.
Use Project Reactor as the reactive stream library for the new reactor-stream processor module (U6), using its windowing/buffering operators for time-window and microbatch features.
Implement the reactor-stream processor as a new XD processor module that uses SpEL/REF-based expression evaluation for field selection and aggregation expressions (min, avg, etc.).
Implement microbatch (U7) using Reactor's buffer(size, timer) operator, exposed as a generic --batchInterval option that can be applied to any source module.
Use Apache Spark's streaming/batch integration via a POC that wraps Spark as a processor or analytics module within Spring XD; identify integration boundary (Spark as a separate worker vs. embedded).
Use Apache JMH for micro-benchmarks and Gatling for end-to-end throughput benchmarks on Rackspace (U8), measuring Kafka producer/consumer baselines first, then XD use-cases.
Documentation (U1) is produced as Markdown pages in the existing XD wiki, organized per module type (source/sink/processor) and per new feature.
assumptions: A single developer is performing all work; 1 workday = 8 productive hours; estimates are effort, not elapsed duration.
The Spring XD codebase, module packaging, and Kafka transport already exist and are stable; this increment extends the platform rather than bootstraps it.
A Kafka cluster and a Spark cluster (or local mode) are available for development and testing.
Rackspace account/credentials and VM provisioning are pre-approved; the developer only needs to set up the VMs and tooling.

User story U2's TBD behavior (resume location on undeployment/redeployment) is interpreted as: 'undeployment releases the explicit start offset; redeploying with a start offset replays from it' — implemented by storing the user-supplied start offset per stream definition and applying it only at initial deploy.
User stories U3 and U4 are treated as related but separate concerns: U3 is the Kafka source-side partition allocation, U4 is the bus-side (transport) allocation across containers.
No major refactoring of the existing XD stream-deployer or Kafka transport is required; new behavior is added through extension points.
Unit tests are written alongside implementation, and an integration test pass at the end covers cross-feature interactions (U32).
Estimates do not include attending meetings, code review feedback cycles with other developers, or production rollout; only the developer-author's work.

activities.activity_description: Define the overall design for the Kafka offset/partition features, the reactor-stream processor, microbatch option, and the Spark integration boundary. Produce a short design note covering APIs, data flow, and persistence.
Configure the XD wiki layout, navigation, and template pages for source, sink, processor and feature documentation (U1).
Write wiki pages documenting how to configure the new and existing XD source modules, including the new Kafka starting offset and batchInterval options (U1, partial).
Write wiki pages documenting how to configure the new and existing XD sink modules (U1).
Write wiki pages documenting processor modules, including the new reactor-stream processor with its time-window and expression options (U1, U6).
Write wiki pages describing the new Kafka offset/partition pre-allocation, reactor-stream, and microbatch features at a conceptual level (U1, U2, U3, U4, U7).
Design how the user-supplied starting offset is captured in the stream definition, persisted per stream, and applied at deploy time without overwriting progress made by already-running modules (U2).

Implement the start-offset parsing in the stream DSL, store it in the deployment metadata, and apply it on the Kafka consumer only when the consumer has no committed offset for the topic-partition (U2).
Write unit and integration tests covering: fresh deploy with start offset, redeploy with start offset (replay), running module crash that does not lose progress, and no start offset supplied (U2).
Design the static assignment algorithm that maps Kafka source module instances to specific topic-partitions at stream deployment time, so that rebalancing does not occur at runtime (U3).
Implement the partition assignment using Kafka's assign() (manual partition assignment) instead of subscribe(), including metadata propagation from the deployer to each source module instance (U3).

Test that the configured Kafka source modules read disjoint partitions, that no group rebalance occurs during a container crash, and that redeploying the stream re-applies the same static assignment (U3).
Design the bus-level (transport) static partition allocation that decides, at stream deploy time, which XD container hosts which transport partitions, independent of the Kafka source U3 logic (U4).
Implement the bus-side allocation in the XD container/runtime so that the bus partitions are pinned to containers at deploy time and a container crash does not trigger a rebalance (U4).
Test that a crashed container's bus partitions are reassigned to the configured target without rebalancing other containers, and that undeployment/redeployment preserves the plan (U4).

Investigate Spark streaming, micro-batch engine, and the available options for embedding Spark as a module vs. running Spark as a separate worker, and survey existing XD/Spark integration patterns (U5).
Design the chosen integration approach, defining the data exchange contract between XD modules and Spark, deployment model, and failure semantics (U5).
Implement a proof-of-concept that ingests data from an XD source, processes it in Spark, and writes results to an XD sink, validating the design (U5).
Document the POC results, the design recommendation, and the next steps for productionizing Spark in XD (U5, also U1).
Design the reactor-stream processor module: DSL options (--timeWindow, --field, --expressions), internal reactor pipeline, and integration with the XD message bus (U6).
Implement the processor module skeleton: option parsing, message-to-Publisher bridge, error handling, and dispatch to the configured operator chain (U6).
Implement the time-window aggregation using Reactor's window/tumbling/buffer operators, supporting the --timeWindow option with min/avg/etc. aggregations (U6).

activities.activity_name: Reactor-stream processor — field and expression evaluation
activities.activity_description: Implement the --field path extraction and the --expressions evaluation (min, avg, etc.) over the selected field within each window (U6).
Test the processor end-to-end on a stream like 'http | reactor-stream --timeWindow=10s --field=payload.sensorData --expressions=min,avg' and on a Kafka source; verify emitted windows (U6).
Design a generic --batchInterval option that can be applied to any source module, using Reactor's buffer(timer) to flush a list of messages at the configured interval (U7).
Implement the batchInterval behavior in the source module base class/option handling, producing a List<Message<?>> per tick downstream (U7).
Test 'http --batchInterval=10 | log' and equivalent Kafka source scenarios, verifying batching and that downstream processors handle list payloads correctly (U7).
Provision Rackspace VMs, configure networking, security groups, and install a baseline OS image for benchmarking (U8).
Install and configure Kafka, Spring XD, JMH, and Gatling on the Rackspace nodes; create scripts to run reproducible benchmark scenarios (U8).
Run Kafka producer/consumer baseline benchmarks to establish a reference, and then run a first set of XD use-case benchmarks (U8).
Document the benchmark setup, how to reproduce results, and the initial baseline numbers in the wiki (U8, U1).

Run an integration suite that exercises a stream combining the new features: Kafka source with start offset + pre-allocated partitions, reactor-stream time window, microbatch, and the Spark POC. Verify offset survival across crashes.
Triage and fix defects found during integration testing, polish error handling, and stabilize the increment for hand-off.
